decision_description: Constitutional violation detected under CLAUDE.md §13.9: the review packet artifact (docs/tier5_deliverables/review_packets/review_packet.json, schema_id orch.tier5.review_packet.v1) asserts specific Horizon Europe programme evaluation rules derived from agent-local knowledge, without traceability to any Tier 1 normative framework source document present and accessible in the repository. Three findings contain specific MSCA-PF evaluation form claims: F-02 asserts the evaluation form 'explicitly requires consideration of the gender dimension and other diversity aspects if relevant for the research project'; F-04 asserts the Impact criterion 'requires assessment of the credibility of the measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher'; F-08 asserts the evaluation form 'specifically notes that institutions holding the HRS4R label are exempted from providing further justification for the Charter alignment criterion.' Each of these is a programme-rule claim that is specific enough to derive from a named Tier 2A or Tier 1 document (the MSCA-PF evaluation form template and/or programme guide), yet no citation to docs/tier1_normative_framework/extracted/ or docs/tier2a_instrument_schemas/extracted/ is embedded in the artifact. The artifact contains no traceability_footer field and therefore no primary_sources[] array providing any Tier 1–4 source anchoring for any finding. §13.9 is unconditional: agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe programme rules may not substitute for Tier 1 source documents when those documents are present and accessible. This violation was identified by the constitutional-compliance-check skill (report_id: compliance_check_review_packet_evaluator_reviewer_2026-07-30T000000Z) as prohibition 13.9 with severity 'major', but no corresponding decision log entry was written by that skill invocation. This entry remedies that gap per CLAUDE.md §9.4.
alternatives_considered: Accept the review packet findings as-is on the basis that MSCA-PF evaluation criteria are publicly known and well-documented programme rules that do not require source citation — rejected because CLAUDE.md §13.9 prohibits agent-local knowledge substitution regardless of the familiarity or public availability of the programme rules; Tier 1 source documents govern unconditionally when present and accessible in the repository.

Treat the §13.9 finding as subsumed by the §13.10 traceability violation already recorded in the decision log, making a separate entry redundant — rejected because §13.9 is a distinct prohibition addressing specifically the substitution of agent knowledge for Tier 1 document reading, whereas §13.10 addresses the absence of Tier 1–4 traceability in the output artifact more broadly; each resolved constitutional finding requires its own durable record per CLAUDE.md §9.4 and §12.3.

Flag the §13.9 finding only in the compliance check validation report and treat the validation report itself as a sufficient durable record — rejected because CLAUDE.md §9.4 requires decisions affecting future interpretation, traceability, or reproducibility to be written to docs/tier4_orchestration_state/decision_log/; a validation report in docs/tier4_orchestration_state/validation_reports/ is a distinct artifact category and does not satisfy the decision log recording requirement.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §13.9 — agents must not use agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe programme rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 source documents when those documents are present and accessible in the repository; Tier 1 normative framework source documents govern when present. Also: CLAUDE.md §9.4 — every decision affecting future interpretation, traceability, or reproducibility must be written to docs/tier4_orchestration_state/decision_log/; decisions held only in agent memory do not constitute durable decisions.
rationale: The evaluator_reviewer agent produced the review packet (docs/tier5_deliverables/review_packets/review_packet.json) as a Phase 8 Tier 5 artifact. Three findings in that artifact — F-02, F-04, and F-08 — assert specific, named MSCA-PF evaluation form requirements: a mandatory gender-dimension sub-criterion, a specific Impact criterion scope formulation, and an HRS4R exemption condition. These assertions are sufficiently specific and verbatim to constitute claims derived from a named Tier 2A or Tier 1 normative document (the MSCA-PF evaluation form template and the Programme Guide General Annexes). The docs/tier2a_instrument_schemas/extracted/ and docs/tier1_normative_framework/extracted/ directories are present in this repository and constitute accessible source documents; §13.9 therefore applies unconditionally. The producing agent did not cite any Tier 1 or Tier 2A source path for these claims, and the artifact carries no traceability_footer. The constitutional-compliance-check skill identified this as a major §13.9 violation but its decision_log_entries_written[] array omitted a §13.9 entry, leaving the violation unrecorded in Tier 4 state in contravention of CLAUDE.md §9.4. This decision log entry closes that gap. Resolution requires the human operator to determine whether the review packet must be revised to embed per-finding Tier 1/2A source citations for all programme-rule assertions, or whether the orch.tier5.review_packet.v1 schema must be amended to include a mandatory traceability_footer with primary_sources[] references anchored to the specific Tier 1 and Tier 2A extracted files from which each evaluator criterion and exemption condition derives.
